LESSON: DEVELOPMENT OF TRANSPORT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities
Topic 3.5: Development of Transport
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Development of Transport, part of Resources and Economic Activities in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is transport important in development?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Development of Transport together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: Learners undertake group activities as they role-play the use of various modern means of

communication.

● Creativity and Imagination: Learners undertake group activities as they role-play use of various modern means of communication.

Values:
● Unity: Learners display team spirit as they role play how to observe traffic rules while using the road.

● Peace: Learners demonstrate love for their own community as they exchange new ideas, draw the road signs in Kenya and display them in

class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Nationalism: Learners display national pride, find out ways of observing road safety in Kenya using digital or print resources and write a report.

● Child road safety: Learners work harmoniously as they role play how to observe traffic rules while using the road.

Link to other subjects

Learners develop acting skills as they role play how to observe traffic rules while using the road.

Suggested Learning Resources

Resource person, maps, tactile maps, digital resources with assistive technology, charts, tactile charts, marker pens, approved text books and other

printed resources or braille resources.
